children: Delhi-based criminal lawyer Vijay Aggarwal, who has represented Mehul Choksi in extradition proceedings, is now accused of rape and faces a charge under the UK's Modern Slavery Act, in addition to the sexual assault counts filed against him in August. Aggarwal, 57, has been in custody in London since his arrest and is set to stand trial at Southwark Crown Court from March 15, 2027.

Prosecutors first flagged the rape allegation in September. It came up as part of new charges at a hearing in London on October 9, where the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) also referred to a charge of arranging or facilitating the travel of another person with a view to exploitation. His personal assistant, Manpreet Kaur, 41, faces a similar charge. A third accused, Hara Tibrewala, pleaded not guilty before Westminster Magistrates' Court and was granted bail on strict conditions, PTI reported.

The case dates back to August 11, when the Metropolitan Police arrested Aggarwal and Kaur at a property on Brick Street in Mayfair after receiving reports of sexual assaults at the address. The alleged incidents are said to have taken place on May 26 and August 9. On August 13, Aggarwal was charged with four counts of sexual assault involving two women. Kaur was charged with two counts of intentionally encouraging or assisting sexual assault. The prosecution alleges that Kaur introduced the women to Aggarwal and invited them to the property after a false job advertisement was posted. Both were remanded in custody by Westminster Magistrates' Court, and Southwark Crown Court rejected Kaur's bail plea on September 4.

At a plea and trial preparation hearing on September 10, CPS barrister Oliver Weetch told Judge Nathaniel Rudolf that the inquiry concerned a series of alleged sexual offences involving three complainants. No pleas were taken because the indictment had not been finalised. Defence barrister Sasha Wass described Aggarwal as a man of “exemplary good character.”

Judge John Milne refused Aggarwal's bail application on September 23. At that hearing, Aggarwal faced 13 counts under the Serious Crime Act and the Modern Slavery Act. The judge held that there was a risk he would leave the country to avoid trial, as his family, business and life were based in India. He called the allegations "deeply disturbing" and referred to a "planned and sinister recruiting campaign" in which young women were allegedly drawn to apply for a purported personal assistant role. He did, however, accept that there was no significant risk of further offending.

The defence had offered security of £230,000 and proposed conditions akin to house arrest. It also cited Aggarwal's health, including a double hernia and kidney problems. Prosecutor Oliver Wellings opposed bail, citing the gravity of the allegations and the strength of the evidence.

Aggarwal, Kaur and Tibrewala were listed to appear before Southwark Crown Court on November 6 for a pre-trial hearing. The trial is expected to last about four weeks. The women who are witnesses in the case are entitled to anonymity under UK law. The allegations against all three accused are yet to be tested at trial. Aggarwal is known for appearing in high-profile white-collar and economic offence cases. He has acted in extradition proceedings in Belgium for Choksi, who is wanted in India in connection with the Punjab National Bank fraud case and has denied the allegations against him.
